_comment: T-2432 (design Sec2.5): one entry per geometry site the four grounding/temper/audit/fold passes found. `family` is R1 (re-derives hidden_size==num_attention_heads*head_dim), QOW (uses hidden_size as a stand-in for q_proj's/o_proj's true width), or KLP (assumes one K-landing path). `status` is fixed, confirmed-correct, rejected (a defined convert/load-time rejection, not a code fix), or not-yet-built (a Track this build did not own). GS-01..GS-04, GS-06..GS-19 are Track A's own scope (T-2432); GS-05 is Track B's (D-SLM5243), out of this ticket's scope and not yet built. GS-26/GS-27 (T-2441) are RunGreedyDecodeLoop/RunGreedyOrDampedGreedyDecodeLoop's own num_attention_heads threading (Critical 1, D-SLM5431). `required_tokens` (T-2441, S2 fix, D-SLM5436): for a `fixed` site, the literal substring(s) that must appear within that occurrence's own bounded scope (see `required_token_scope_ends`, below). Present ONLY on `fixed` sites: `confirmed-correct` sites are intentionally unchanged by this ask (their own governing quantity is correctly hidden_size/intermediate_size, not q_width), so a presence check would be backwards for them, and `not-yet-built` sites have no code to check yet. Derived once, by reading each site's own diff against v1.3.0 (2f225fc..327ee29) -- see tools/geometry_site_census.py's own module docstring for how the census applies this field. `require_all_tokens` (T-2445, default false/absent): when a site's own required_tokens are ALTERNATE spellings of the same quantity at different occurrences (the default, OR semantics -- any one satisfies), this stays false/absent; when a site's ONE occurrence governs several independent sub-assignments that would otherwise share one generic token (GS-18), this is true and required_tokens holds one EXACT fragment per sub-assignment (AND semantics -- all must be present, so reverting any one is caught by that one fragment going missing). `required_token_scope_end_offsets` (T-2475, Claude/Poirot/6597903-t2472-ask5-tracka-confirmation.md, Significant 1; supersedes `required_token_scope_ends`, T-2445): a map from `"relative/path.ext:occurrence_ordinal"` (forward slashes; occurrence_ordinal is 0-based, this site's Nth marker for THIS gs_id found in THIS file, in ascending line order -- stable under any edit that does not reorder this site's own markers relative to each other) to the OFFSET, in lines, from that occurrence's own marker to the LAST line of that occurrence's own governed code, or `null` if that occurrence has no independently-revertible code of its own (a declaration whose own text never changes regardless of what a sibling occurrence assigns it -- GS-08's forward_sites.h occurrence). Replaces the prior absolute-line keying (`required_token_scope_ends`, `"relative/path.ext:marker_line"` -> absolute end line), which the T-2467 round ruled self-detecting on the reasoning that census.py recomputes the LOOKUP key's marker_line fresh every run -- true, and irrelevant, because the STORED key and the stored end line were both absolute line numbers frozen at authoring time, so an edit anywhere ELSE in the same file (the reviewer's own construction: one comment line at the very top of the file, nowhere near any marker) shifted the marker's own current line without shifting the registry's committed key or value to match, producing a false MISSING/mismatched-scope failure on untouched, correctly-fixed code -- foreshadowed at GS-01, whose own note below records exactly this shape being hit and hand-repaired once already (T-2450's 8-line insert), and reproduced on demand as the general case by Claude/Poirot/6597903-t2472-ask5-tracka-confirmation.md Sec4. The offset scheme closes this: occurrence_ordinal depends only on how many of this site's OWN markers precede this one in the file, which an edit elsewhere cannot change, and offset is the LOCAL distance from marker to governed code, invariant under any edit outside that local span. An edit INSIDE an occurrence's own governed span (between its marker and its own required token) can still desync the offset -- unchanged from the prior scheme, and not the class either scheme was built to close. census.py fails closed (a REGRESSED SITE, or MISSING required_token_scope_end_offsets ENTRY, report) rather than silently, on drift or on a new occurrence added without one.
